questions.question: What is the key on a map, and why does a farming map need one?
questions.expected_answer: The key, or legend, is a box that shows each symbol on the map and explains what it means. A farming map needs a key so that readers know which symbol stands for which crop or animal.

questions.question: Name the main areas where maize, sugar cane and sheep are farmed in South Africa.
questions.expected_answer: Maize is grown mainly in the Free State, North West and Mpumalanga. Sugar cane is grown in KwaZulu-Natal and the Lowveld of Mpumalanga. Sheep are kept mainly in the dry Karoo, in the Eastern Cape, Northern Cape and Western Cape, and in the Free State.

questions.question: Explain the pattern of farming between the east and the west of South Africa.
questions.expected_answer: The east of South Africa gets more rain than the west. So most crops are grown in the wetter east and where there is irrigation, while sheep and goats are kept in the drier centre and west, where crops cannot grow without irrigation.
